transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Welcome in. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what made me come in today is that I've been having some trouble at work. I'm a receptionist, and lately, I've started losing my place while I'm scheduling appointments or, you know, working on the lobby displays. It's like my mind just slips off track because I'm busy thinking about what I might have overlooked. It's getting frustrating to deal with.

When you find yourself thinking about what you might have overlooked, does it feel more like a general worry that's hard to stop, or more like a specific unwanted thought that makes you feel you need to go back and check something?

It's more of a general worry that's hard to stop. I mean, I can tell myself, "Sunny, it's handled," but the thought just keeps looping. And pretty soon I've gone from one concern to another, until I'm just checking details in my head over and over. It's not really that I have to physically go back and check things, it just keeps running through my mind.

Sunny, how long have you been experiencing this constant worrying and trouble concentrating—has it been going on for several months or more, or did it start more recently after some particular event or change in your life?

It's been going on for about nine months now. It actually started right after... well, I had an overnight detention, and there was a whole paperwork mix-up around it. Ever since that happened, the worrying has just kind of stuck with me.

Sunny, aside from worries connected to that detention and paperwork mix-up, do you find yourself worrying excessively about other things too—like your health, finances, family, or other everyday matters?

Yeah, I do. It's not just about that one incident anymore. I find myself worrying about all kinds of just... ordinary things now. Like work schedules, paying bills, travel plans, or even just little paperwork errors at the desk. It's like I have this constant feeling that one small mix-up is going to snowball and turn into a much bigger problem.
Since that detention incident nine months ago, have you experienced any unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about it that make you feel like you're re-living the event?
No, I haven't had anything like that. I don't have nightmares about it or feel like I'm reliving it. It's really just the worrying that stuck around, not memories of the actual night.

latest_inference.note: Absence of flashbacks, nightmares, or re-experiencing symptoms rules out PTSD (F43.1). The worry has generalized beyond the initial incident to multiple domains (work, finances, travel) and has persisted for 9 months, consistent with Generalized Anxiety Disorder rather than Adjustment Disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports approximately 9 months of excessive, difficult-to-control worry spanning multiple domains (work, finances, travel, paperwork errors), accompanied by concentration difficulty (losing place at work) and looping cognitive worry rather than intrusive obsessions or compulsive checking behaviors. Although symptoms emerged after a stressful event (overnight detention), there are no re-experiencing symptoms (no flashbacks, nightmares, intrusive memories), avoidance, or hyperarousal symptoms required for PTSD, and the worry generalized beyond the index event, arguing against PTSD/Adjustment Disorder. The clinical picture—chronic, multi-domain, free-floating worry with cognitive interference—best fits Generalized Anxiety Disorder.
